# Template: event_study
An event-study plot: estimated coefficients as dots with confidence- interval whiskers at each event time, a dashed zero line, a dashed vertical treatment line, the reference period pinned at zero, flat (or deliberately violated) pre-trends, and a post-treatment effect that can be immediate or ramp up. The signature figure of modern applied economics. Choose this scene for ANY request about event studies, dynamic difference-in-differences coefficients, pre-trends or pre-trend tests, treatment-effect dynamics around a policy change, or coefficient-with-confidence-interval plots over event time. This is a SCHEMATIC — the coefficients are generated from shape knobs, not read from a coefficient vector — but `effect`, `pre_trend` and `ci` take a code element's variable via a "{id.var}" token, so the size of the jump and the width of the whiskers can be what a regression in Python actually estimated. A token must arrive already on THIS figure's scale: `effect` is CLAMPED to -3..3, `ci` to 0.1..1 and `pre_trend` to -0.5..0.5, silently, so have the script rescale first (divide a dollar effect by its own standard deviation, say) — an unscaled coefficient pins to the edge and draws a confident-looking figure that is wrong. `periods_pre` and `periods_post` stay typed integers (they set the window, they are not data); until the script has run the figure draws its default schematic, so every coef_i beat already exists.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "periods_pre": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "Event times before treatment, 2-8 (default 5)."
  },
  "periods_post": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "Event times from treatment on, 2-8 (default 5)."
  },
  "effect": {
   "oneOf": [
    {
     "type": "number",
     "description": "Post-treatment effect size, -3..3 (default 1)."
    },
    {
     "type": "string",
     "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
    }
   ]
  },
  "ramp": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Effect grows linearly over post periods instead of jumping (default false)."
  },
  "pre_trend": {
   "oneOf": [
    {
     "type": "number",
     "description": "Slope of a pre-trend VIOLATION, -0.5..0.5 (default 0 = clean flat pre-trends)."
    },
    {
     "type": "string",
     "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
    }
   ]
  },
  "ci": {
   "oneOf": [
    {
     "type": "number",
     "description": "Confidence-interval half-width, 0.1-1 (default 0.35)."
    },
    {
     "type": "string",
     "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
    }
   ]
  },
  "y_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Default \"Effect\"."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the coordinate axes (a group with captions)
- zero_line: dashed horizontal line at zero
- treat_line: dashed vertical line where treatment begins (with its caption)
- coef_<i>: coefficient dot + CI whisker at event time i (a group, in time order from the earliest)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw an event-study plot with flat pre-trends and a clear treatment effect." → params: {"title":"Event study"}
Request: "Show an event study where the pre-trends are violated." → params: {"pre_trend":0.25,"title":"When pre-trends fail"}

In YAML: `template: event_study` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
